principle: Distinguish mathematical proof under assumptions, architectural invariants, source observations, local tests, and open proof obligations. Never infer a general implementation from a formal operator definition.

claims.claim: For the stated finite, pure and total fragment (Id, Call, Seq, If, finite Map, Verify), well-typed input terminates with a result of the declared type or an explicitly typed error.
assumptions: finite registry of pure total components obeying signatures
claims.scope: the finite fragment stated in the theorem; not all operators/effects/concurrency/recursion
claims.evidence: theory section 'Propriétés et obligations de vérification' and theorem proof

claims.claim: Sequential contract composition is valid when the first postcondition entails the second precondition and output/input types match.
assumptions: correct Hoare-style contracts for both components
claims.scope: contract composition; guarantees depend on component contracts being true

claims.claim: An equitable, resumable search eventually examines any reachable candidate at finite rank under finite predecessor and positive continuing resource assumptions.
assumptions: finite predecessor set for each finite-rank candidate
claims.scope: eventual examination; no finite time bound or guarantee for arbitrary infinite/unreachable spaces
claims.evidence: proposition on search fairness in theory

claims.claim: Hibernate/wake can reduce resident working-set memory, but does not by itself reduce the number of candidates in the logical search space.
assumptions: cold payload remains recoverable; lifecycle protocol preserves exact state
claims.evidence: sections on combinatorial explosion and sleep/wake

claims.claim: Lossless compression must preserve canonical reconstruction and content hash; a lossy summary must retain a pointer to the exact source and declare its fidelity domain.
assumptions: canonical serializer and cryptographic hash are used consistently
claims.scope: integrity/fidelity contract; it does not prove semantic utility of lossy summaries
claims.evidence: operator semantics table and living-memory rules

claims.claim: Typed information waves are durable software events, not a physical wave mechanism; delivery requires provenance, idempotency/deduplication and bounded fan-out/TTL/backpressure.
assumptions: persistent store and idempotency policy behave according to contract
claims.scope: protocol specification plus local prototype subset; generic application handlers remain outside prototype
claims.evidence: theory operator semantics; living composition runtime

claims.claim: The theory grammar's operators have explicit target contracts and are mapped to architecture/prototype status.
assumptions: coverage is defined at specification level, not equated with implementation
claims.scope: 29 constructors in grammar and integration matrix
claims.evidence: grammar, semantic table and FulleGenBrain_3 matrix

claims.claim: A general proof that every compiled program is observationally equivalent to interpreter execution is not established in this release.
claims.scope: full compiler/runtime, effects, concurrency, exceptions and persistence semantics
claims.evidence: explicitly retained as open obligation; no proof assistant run claimed

claims.claim: The reference runtime implements all theoretical composition operators.
claims.scope: explicitly not claimed; runtime is partial by documented matrix
claims.evidence: matrix marks AST interpreter, generic synthesis, transform, observation/probe, transactions and several operators not integrated

claims.claim: The local regression suite passes in the recorded environment.
assumptions: Python/pytest environment used for this release
claims.scope: 31 tests for the two prototype modules; not end-to-end FGB3 validation

source_provenance: sources/evidence/source_manifest.json; historical O62/O63 results are archival evidence, not newly executed experiments.
